scope: Proposition 8.10 (Average correction from one fixed radius) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 96. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed template there is ρ > 0 such that the following holds for all sufficiently large sizes. Let a received balanced word w satisfy dist(w, W) ≤ ρ, where W is structurally canonical; validity of its label is not needed here. For every fixed Creq < ∞ and η > 0, a bounded-bit algorithm predicts requests with outer density at most Creq with average error at most η. It has smooth potential raw reads on every fixed hypothetical answer branch. The radius is independent of Creq, η, the row-round count, and the subsequent amplification count.
